record.original_question: In the extremal cases where the non-negative rank of the average mixing matrix Mc or the completely positive semidefinite rank of Mc attains its extreme value, determine what combinatorial consequences can be deduced for the underlying graph.

evidence.quote: In each of these cones of matrices, it is natural and often very useful to find the rank within the cone of a given matrix.
4.4 Open Problem. In the extremal cases for the non-negative or cpsd ranks, what combinatorial consequences may be derived?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a finite simple graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A, and let H(t) = exp(itA) be the associated continuous-time quantum walk transition matrix. The average mixing matrix of X is defined by
  M_X = lim_{T→∞} (1/T) ∫_0^T H(t) ∘ H(−t) dt,
where ∘ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. Equivalently, if A has spectral decomposition A = Σ_r λ_r E_r with the E_r being the orthogonal projections onto the eigenspaces, then
  M_X = Σ_r E_r ∘ E_r.
The matrix M_X is symmetric, doubly stochastic, and positive semidefinite with rational entries.

Recall:
(a) The non-negative rank rank_+(M) of an entrywise non-negative matrix M is the smallest k such that M = Σ_{i=1}^{k} u_i v_i^T with u_i, v_i entrywise non-negative.
(b) The completely positive semidefinite (cpsd) rank cpsd-rank(M) of a matrix M that admits a Gram representation by positive semidefinite matrices is the smallest d such that M_{ij} = tr(P_i P_j) for some d×d positive semidefinite matrices P_1,…,P_n.

Both rank_+(M_X) and cpsd-rank(M_X) are bounded above by n, and standard inequalities give various lower bounds in terms of rank(M_X).

Problem. Suppose that rank_+(M_X) (respectively cpsd-rank(M_X)) attains an extremal value (for instance equals rank(M_X), or equals n). Determine the combinatorial structure of the graph X that is forced by such an extremal equality. In particular, characterize the family of graphs X for which rank_+(M_X) equals its minimum possible value rank(M_X), and the family of graphs X for which cpsd-rank(M_X) equals rank(M_X).
artifact.category_tag: Average mixing matrices of quantum walks
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface any work resolving the combinatorial characterization of graphs whose average mixing matrix attains extremal non-negative rank or extremal completely positive semidefinite rank. The non-negative rank and cpsd-rank are known to be hard to compute in general, and while the average mixing matrix has been studied (Godsil and collaborators), no characterization tying its extremal cone-ranks to graph-theoretic structure appears in the literature found. The status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Average mixing of continuous quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: Defines and studies the average mixing matrix of a graph derived from continuous-time quantum walks.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the average mixing matrix as a graph invariant whose entries encode long-time behavior of quantum walks.

status_evidence.title: Completely Positive Semidefinite Rank
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the cpsd-rank of matrices, showing it is in general hard to compute and bounded below by usual rank.
status_evidence.claim: The cpsd-rank is a refined matrix parameter for which extremal values impose strong structural constraints, but no graph-theoretic characterization for average mixing matrices is given.

status_evidence.title: Nonnegative rank (linear algebra) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Definitions and basic properties of non-negative rank, noting it is NP-hard to compute in general.
status_evidence.claim: No general combinatorial characterization is known for the equality of non-negative rank and ordinary rank for matrices arising from graph invariants such as the average mixing matrix.
